{{Quote|The Empire ordered us to move on. To reinforce loyal troops, fighting just south of us. We were not to leave any troops behind as guards for the prisoners&mdash;and certainly we were not to leave any of them living.''"<br />"''They didn't tell you to execute the prisoners.''"<br />"''They didn't have to. It took almost five minutes, Fett. We put them in a holding pen and started shooting at them. They screamed and screamed and screamed. We just kept shooting until the screaming had stopped. I was following orders.|Kardue'sai'Malloc and Boba Fett|<ref name="The Last One Standing" />}}
'''Kardue'sai'Malloc''' was a [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] [[Devaronian Army|army]] [[Captain/Legends|captain]] and devoted [[Music/Legends|music]] aficionado with a massive collection of rare recordings. When his unit was deployed against a rebellion on [[Devaron/Legends|Devaron]], Malloc captured seven hundred rebel [[Gender/Legends|men]], women, and children in the city of [[Montellian Serat/Legends|Montellian Serat]] and shelled the city. Interpreting his orders to move on without the prisoners as double-speak ordering their executions, he had all the prisoners rounded up and [[Death/Legends|killed]], earning him the nickname "'''The Butcher of Montellian Serat'''."

Malloc resigned from the military and fled his [[Planet/Legends|world's]] retribution, spending years following his favorite musical performers across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and avoiding [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] seeking to collect the five-million-[[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credit]] bounty placed on him. He eventually settled on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where he lived under the alias "'''Labria'''" and made a living as an [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]]. Regarded as the worst [[Spy/Legends|spy]] in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]], he spent most of his time [[Alcohol/Legends|drunk]] in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]]. When [[Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes/Legends|Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes]], one of Malloc's favorite groups, arrived on Tatooine in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], he masterminded an elaborate scheme to steal them from [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt's]] employ and force them into a contract playing at Chalmun's.

When a chance encounter with a Devaronian [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] in [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]] caused him to be recognized, Malloc killed the mercenary and his companions and fled to [[Peppel]], a remote world. He lived behind tight security, knowing that renowned bounty hunter [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] was on his trail; Fett finally tracked Malloc down and captured him in [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]]. Malloc was returned to Devaron, where his family and several thousand Devaronians watched approvingly as he was cast into a pit of starving [[quarra]] and consumed alive.

==Biography==
===Becoming the Butcher===
{{Quote|Our orders came just after noon. The Rebels were believed to be moving north; I was to take my forces and intercept them. I was not to leave any of my forces behind as guards for the captured Rebels. The orders were no more specific than that&hellip;but they could not be misunderstood.|Kardue'sai'Malloc|<ref name="Empire Blues" />}}
Kardue'sai'Malloc, born to the [[Kardue family]] of [[Devaron/Legends|Devaron]], was the third member thereof to carry his name.<ref name="Empire Blues" /> He had at least one brother growing up.<ref name="The Last One Standing" /> The Kardues had a long and proud tradition of military service stretching back sixteen generations, one which Malloc decided to carry on. He joined the [[Devaronian Army]], rising to the rank of [[Captain/Legends|captain]]. Military life agreed with Malloc, aside from the necessity of putting [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] [[Troop/Legends|troops]] under [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] command when the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] reached Devaron.<ref name="Empire Blues" />

Malloc was a fanatic lover of [[Music/Legends|music]] and an avid collector of recordings. He built up a vast library of musical recordings by famed artists over the years. Many of his copies were rare and expensive; some were the sole existing recordings of a particular performance. Music was his great passion and what he considered to be his reason for living and could achieve transcendent experiences listening to beloved recordings.<ref name="Empire Blues" /> A great many of his recordings were of music suppressed and destroyed by the Empire as seditious.<ref name="The Last One Standing" /> Malloc married, producing a daughter, [[Mika'sai'Malloc]], though he was not close with his family.<ref name="The Last One Standing" /><ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>

When the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]] sprang up on Devaron, Malloc's unit was among those combating it under the direction of the Empire's forces. He commanded the siege of the ancient city of [[Montellian Serat/Legends|Montellian Serat]], where a group of Rebels had fortified themselves. Malloc shelled the city overnight, at dawn offering a chance to surrender. The seven hundred beleaguered Rebels accepted, and Malloc placed them under guard in a holding pen he had erected. A group of Rebels was still fighting not far to the south, and Malloc feared a possible rescue attempt. On Imperial orders, he shelled Montellian Serat to rubble in order to make an example. At noon that same day he received orders from his Imperial commanders to intercept the second group of Rebels, which was moving north; he was not to leave guards behind for the captured Rebels. Malloc interpreted this as very clear double-speak ordering him to execute the prisoners, which he did, having his guards open fire. Within five minutes all seven hundred were [[Death/Legends|dead]] and, leaving them unburied, Malloc proceeded to the next battle.<ref name="Empire Blues" />

Malloc knew that this act had effectively ended his military career. Six months later, when the Rebels were finally eliminated entirely, he submitted his resignation. Reviled among his people as a war criminal, he knew he would be put on trial with his resignation; he also knew that his request to resign could make him guilty of [[Treason/Legends|treason]] against the Empire. With his choices equally bad, he was indifferent to the outcome; he simply had no desire to stay in the army. His resignation was accepted and he vanished before anyone could take action against him, leaving his family behind.<ref name="Empire Blues" />

===Tatooinian exile===
{{Quote|There are downsides to being safe, though. The closest Devish woman is on the other side of the Core. Just the thought makes my horns ache.|Kardue'sai'Malloc|<ref name="Empire Blues" />}}
[[File:Labria-GG1.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Malloc living on Tatooine under the alias "Labria".]]
The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] placed a five million [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credit]] bounty on Malloc, who had acquired the epithet "The Butcher of Montellian Serat".<ref name="Fact File">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 138|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 138]]</ref><ref name="Empire Blues" /> This was a significant sum, enough to incite [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] himself to pursue Malloc during the [[The galaxy/Legends|Galactic]] Civil War, though he was persuaded to seek other quarry.<ref name="The Hunger">''[[Galaxy of Fear: The Hunger]]''</ref><ref name="The Last One Standing" /> Malloc took his vast music collection with him when he left and used his flight to further his great passion, seeing various artists on tour. He considered there to be no more than six great living artists he had never seen live. He spent five years following [[Maxa Jandovar]], a noted [[vandfill]]ist and political opponent of the Empire, on her informal tour, but always missed her. Malloc was on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] preparing to follow her to [[Morvogodine]] when he heard that she had been arrested and died in custody there.<ref name="Empire Blues" /><ref name="Star Wars Blog Slugthrower">{{SW|url=news/slugthrowers-part-2|series=Slugthrowers: An Overview of Popular Music and Musicians in a Galaxy Far, Far Away|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref>

Malloc stayed on Tatooine, where he lived under the alias of "Labria" to avoid [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]]. The term was an obscene one in [[Devaronese/Legends|Devaronese]], meaning "cold food". He had not originally intended to stay there, but simply never left, eventually settling down for good in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]]; he did consider his distance from Devaron and relative anonymity as distinct advantages in staying safe. He became a regular patron of [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] despite his profound distaste for the musical entertainment offered and was regularly the first patron in the door on mornings. He regarded the [[Bartender/Legends|bartender]] there, [[Wuher/Legends|Wuher]], as his best friend. He enjoyed Wuher's general distaste for the universe at large and considered him something of a kindred spirit; Wuher regarded "Labria" as a friend as well and was sometimes amused at Malloc's continual jokes. Malloc spent much of his time in the cantina drinking; the cantina claimed to supply his favorite [[Alcohol/Legends|alcohol]], [[Merenzane Gold/Legends|Merenzane Gold]]. Though the substance was not genuine Merenzane Gold, he drank it anyway.<ref name="Empire Blues" />

Malloc kept an apartment near the cantina. Used to a cold environment on Devaron, it was heavily cooled. Malloc maintained a sanctuary in a secret room behind the [[Refresher/Legends|refresher]] where he stored his massive music collection and to which he retreated after days at the cantina to enjoy musical bliss.<ref name="Empire Blues" /> He kept his finances, some five thousand credits, in a bank account under the reverse of his alias&mdash;"Airbal".<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" />

Malloc took up the trade of an [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]], [[Spy/Legends|spying]] and picking up tidbits of information, though he never bothered to verify his sources; he readily admitted that he was not much good at it, and his peers agreed. Local crimelord [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] referred to Malloc as his "least favorite spy" but occasionally took information from him. Malloc used his reputation as a perpetual drunkard to his advantage, frequently faking inebriation to gain information. Malloc was able to make some money through the occupation, frequently selling information about Jabba to [[Garindan/Legends|Garindan]], the preeminent spy in Mos Eisley. The information generally turned out useless; each blamed the other for mishandling the tips, but Malloc continued to be Garindan's primary source for reports about Jabba.<ref name="Empire Blues" /><ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /> At one point, he became involved in a scam in which he and [[Oxbel]], one of only two other Devaronians on Tatooine, pretended to be brothers who had arrived on Tatooine for gambling purposes; the scam did not play out.<ref name="Empire Blues" /><ref name="Galaxy Guide 7">''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]''</ref>

===The Modal Nodes scam===
{{Quote|Lab&hellip;if you put this kind of effort into anything else, you could be a wealthy being.''"<br />"''My friend, this is all that I want.|Wuher and Kardue'sai'Malloc|<ref name="Empire Blues" />}}
One day in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Malloc was approached by Garindan, who told Malloc that he wanted to sell him information. He quickly realized that it regarded music and readily paid the fifty credits the other spy demanded. When Garindan revealed his information, Malloc was ecstatic to learn that [[Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes/Legends|Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes]] were on Tatooine, playing for Jabba the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]. Malloc regarded them as the greatest [[Jizz/Legends|jizz]] band in the galaxy and was determined to see them. Returning to his apartment at the end of the day, he played Modal Nodes recordings in anticipation of seeing them perform.<ref name="Empire Blues" />

The next day, Malloc went to see the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]. He offered Jabba the services of [[Obron Mettlo]], a [[Moorin]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] he had encountered the previous day. The crimelord agreed, and Malloc promised to bring Mettlo by for dinner and entertainment; Jabba told Malloc that he was not invited to the meeting. Morose at his inability to see the band, Malloc went back to Chalmun's Cantina and drank, dreading the thought of the Hutt, whose musical tastes he did not regard highly, feeding the band to his [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]]. When he heard that Jabba loved the Modal Nodes, Malloc was even more despondent at the fact that they were playing regular engagements nearby and he had no way of seeing them. After five days of bitterness and heavy drinking, Malloc was beaten and robbed in an alleyway behind the cantina while inebriated. Wuher found him and carried him back to his apartment, where Malloc spent the whole night, depressed, in the cold shower.<ref name="Empire Blues" />

Feeling horrible, Malloc did not leave his apartment for days, recovering. He was frightened to go outdoors, fearing that he would be preyed upon as a weakling if news got out of his mugging. When his arm had finally healed weeks later, he ventured out; his food supply was running low. Going to the cantina early as was his custom, he was greeted by Wuher as the first patron. His friend offered him a drink on the house, and Malloc was completely shocked to find that Wuher had presented him with a glass of genuine Merenzane Gold as a welcome-back gift. He savored the drink while he caught up on the news&mdash;Mettlo had picked a fight with some other guards and been killed, worrying Malloc that Jabba might seek retribution. When Garindan mentioned that Lady [[Valarian/Legends|Valarian]], the Hutt's local rival, was getting married, Malloc had an idea come to him.<ref name="Empire Blues" />

He approached Wuher and asked if the bartender would like to have quality live entertainment cheap and explained his plan; Wuher agreed. Malloc approached Valarian and convinced her to hire the Modal Nodes for her wedding, playing on her desire to outdo Jabba. He sent a messenger droid to the Modal Nodes recruiting them, and on the morning of the wedding he tipped Jabba off to the fact that the band was working Valarian's wedding. He gave Wuher the invitation to the wedding that Valarian had provided him, and instructed him to bring the band back and offer them a contract when Jabba had the wedding broken up. The plan went off perfectly, with Malloc watching the wedding and tripping the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] who came after Wuher and the Modal Nodes during their escape. As part of their deal, Malloc received seven free drinks a day as long as they played; he extended the likelihood of their staying longer by winning the band's instruments in a game of [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] with [[Figrin D'an/Legends|Figrin D'an]], played using cards marked in the infrared spectrum, which Devaronians could see but [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] could not. Malloc was annoyed with the first day of music,<ref name="Empire Blues" /> which was interrupted by fights involving [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]],<ref name="A New Hope" /> but as the evening approached the Modal Nodes hit their stride, knowing they had a dedicated fan in the audience who actually appreciated their music. Malloc's plan had played out perfectly.<ref name="Empire Blues" />

A short time afterwards, Malloc accompanied the [[Stennes Shifter/Legends|Stennes Shifter]] [[Trinto Duaba/Legends|Trinto Duaba]] to his favorite cantina during the night shift. However, an Imperial curfew had been enacted on the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo system]], and the cantina was closed. The night shift bartender, [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena]], attempted to deny Malloc entry, but he did not accept her decision and pulled a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster]] to force his way in. The [[Bouncer (occupation)/Legends|bouncer]] [[Tork]] attempted to intervene, but Ackmena stopped him from throwing them out, wanting no more violence during her shift. Ackmena was eventually able to get Malloc and the other customers out of the cantina by singing the song [[Goodnight, But Not Goodbye/Legends|''Goodnight, But Not Goodbye'']], accompanied by the Modal Nodes.<ref name="The Star Wars Holiday Special">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref><ref name="Star Wars Blog Holiday">{{SW|url=news/the-star-wars-holiday-special-cantina-we-may-not-thrive-friend-but-we-survive-friend|text=''The Star Wars Holiday Special'' Cantina: Who's Who|int=The Star Wars Holiday Special Cantina: Who's Who|nolive=1}}</ref>

===Manipulating the situation===
{{Quote|It is said in Mos Eisley that you cannot trust Labria as far as Long Snoot can throw him.|Voren Na'al|<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" />}}
[[File:LabriaEGC.jpg|thumb|200px|Kardue'sai'Malloc]]
Malloc was occasionally employed by [[Slag Flats]], a small-time local crimelord. She was a friend of [[Adar Tallon/Legends|Adar Tallon]], who was in hiding on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. When the search for Tallon reached Tatooine shortly after Malloc executed the Modal Nodes scam, Malloc came across a party of individuals seeking Tallon. He arranged a rendezvous later in which he led them from the [[Spaceport Hotel]] to [[Tower Ridge]] on his [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]]. He directed them to an unused water silo where Flats would be and departed. Malloc was actually in the employ of [[Jodo Kast]], a bounty hunter seeking Tallon, and the rival party was ambushed at the water silo.<ref name="Tatooine Manhunt">''[[Tatooine Manhunt]]''</ref>

Malloc learned that Kast had killed Flats, which he regretted. However, he remained on Kast's side and sent a note to the party, which had survived, asking them to meet with [[Arno (Tatooinian)|Arno]], one of Tallon's friends, in the cantina. When they arrived, Kast's team of hunters was also present, and Malloc pointed out the targets and quickly got out of the way as the party was attacked, though he was wounded in the firefight. When the group returned from rescuing Tallon from Kast in the desert, Malloc tipped off [[Prefect/Legends|Prefect]] [[Orun Depp]] and watched as they were attacked, though the group escaped Tatooine.<ref name="Tatooine Manhunt" /> Whether for this Imperial assistance or other offenses, [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] listed "Labria" as a target of opportunity.<ref name="TCG">{{JKTCG|set=Premiere|cardname=Labria • Slippery Informant|link=http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/cardlists/premier/large/114RRlabriaslippery.html}}</ref>

When Mos Eisley authorities picked up smuggling kingpin [[Big Bunji/Legends|Big Bunji]], with whom Malloc had previously done some business, on minor charges, Malloc saw an opportunity to seize Bunji's cargo of valuable [[Espionage matrix|espionage matrices]] for spy droids. He tried to engage a group of spacers to steal the cargo for him, but was interrupted by the arrival of Bunji's agents [[Voushon]], [[Wrex]], and [[Rait]]. They dragged him outside, but Malloc insisted he had not been the one to tip off the police about Bunji, and they let him go.<ref name="Many a Slip">{{WEGCite|story=There's Many a Slip Betwixt Cup and Lip|book=Mos Eisley Adventure Set}}</ref>

The spacers ended up working for Voushon, agreeing to break Bunji out of the [[Mos Eisley Police Station]] in exchange for a cut of the hidden cargo. Malloc collaborated with Garindan to track down the matrices, trailing the spacers and, when they noticed him, distracting them with an offer to join forces long enough for Garindan's agents to plant a comlink on one of the group. They rejected his offer, and Garindan disrupted their efforts to rescue Bunji, receiving a payoff from the new prefect, [[Eugene Talmont]]. The Empire failed to prevent Bunji's escape, however, and the spacers gained their profit while Malloc's plans were foiled.<ref name="Many a Slip" />

===Exile ended===
{{Quote|By the Cold. I can't believe I got caught by a nerf herder like you.|Kardue'sai'Malloc, to Boba Fett|<ref name="The Last One Standing" />}}
Malloc entertained some ambitions of selling his skills to the Empire once more as an Imperial agent, though never seriously acted on them.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /> With the Empire's decline after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], however, that opportunity was closed, as was his major income source&mdash;Jabba was killed around the same time, rendering his supply of information about the Hutt unneeded. He remained quietly on Tatooine.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Characters">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Eventually, in [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]], four mercenaries entered the cantina, one of the two Devaronians among them recognized him as Malloc, and they attempted to take the bounty on his head. By now old but still deadly, Malloc killed them and left the planet.<ref name="The Last One Standing" />

Malloc made his way to [[Peppel]], a remote world where he set up an extensive security system around his simple hut, which did not even have indoor plumbing. He lived off Merenzane Gold and animals he hunted himself; his music collection was buried in a case in the yard. Having heard that legendary bounty hunter Boba Fett was after him, he lived far more carefully than he had on Tatooine, hiding behind the intense security and carrying an assault rife even to go to the pit toilet he had dug outside. He lived this way for two years, remaining wary.<ref name="The Last One Standing" />

In [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], Fett tracked Malloc to Peppel, where he observed him and prepared an ambush. When Malloc left the hut in the evening to relieve himself, Fett shot him in the shoulder with an arrow&mdash;one of the few weapons he could get past Malloc's sensors. As Malloc fell, Fett hamstrung him and forced him to surrender. Malloc was bound and taken into the hut, where he refused to cooperate with Fett and pushed the bounty hunter to kill him. As the bounty was for live capture only, Fett refused. Malloc attempted to barter his music collection for his life; when that failed he made Fett promise to dig it up and sell it to a contact he would provide,<ref name="The Last One Standing" /> the director of the [[Coruscant University School of Music]].<ref name="Star Wars Blog Slugthrower" /> He also demanded that Fett bring six bottles of his stock of Merenzane Gold along.<ref name="The Last One Standing" />

Malloc was kept in a cell aboard the ''[[Slave IV]]'' for the trip to Devaron; he finished the first five bottles early on. His shoulder wound healed, but his leg became infected and could not be treated. Meanwhile, Malloc spent the entire trip dreading what awaited him&mdash;execution by [[quarra]]. He would be thrown to a pit of the starving hunting beasts, which would eat him alive. Due to Devaronian resiliency, he would be awake and aware through most of it. When they were finally ready to arrive, Fett restrained Malloc and gave him the final bottle of alcohol. When they arrived, he was identified by his daughter as Kardue'sai'Malloc; neither displayed any emotion toward the other.<ref name="The Last One Standing" />

Malloc was turned over to the Devaronian authorities. Utterly terrified but enjoying one last view of the world he missed for so many decades, he was taken before a massive crowd of ten thousand Devaronians at [[Judgment Field]] in the ruins of Montellian Serat, accompanied by his daughter and brother.<ref name="The Last One Standing" /> His wife, refusing to have anything to do with him, did not attend.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> As he was thrown to the quarra, he enjoyed the scenery and made an effort to arch his neck back so the quarra would tear out his throat and let him die quickly.<ref name="The Last One Standing" /> In the pit, he struggled briefly before dying.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

He was survived by his music, which Fett did distribute to his contact.<ref name="The Last One Standing" /> The School of Music on Coruscant disseminated Malloc's collection into the larger galaxy.<ref name="Star Wars Blog Slugthrower" /> Music long suppressed by the Empire, preserved only by Malloc, was published to be enjoyed by the galaxy.<ref name="The Last One Standing" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|My people believe that to kill something, you must cherish it and love it as it dies. There is no barrier between you and the thing you are killing, and you die as you kill. Music is the only thing I know that feels the same way. The music surrounds me until I cease to exist. I die as I kill. It's what I live for. I'm glad my fathers are dead.|Kardue'sai'Malloc|<ref name="Empire Blues" />}}
[[File:Malloc_SWGTCG-AoD.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Malloc raises a glass in Chalmun's Cantina.]]
A [[Gender/Legends|male]] of the [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] [[Species/Legends|species]],<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /> which was heavily differentiated by sex, Kardue'sai'Malloc had a genetic trait possessed by around one in fifty Devaronian men: two sets of [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]]. While his inner row of teeth were sharp canines, the outer row consisted of flat "female" teeth that were retractable, whether intentionally or as a reflex action when threatened or angry.<ref name="Empire Blues" /> He had [[Color/Legends|brown]] skin and red-brown eyes.<ref name="A New Hope" />

Malloc had a tremendous love for music; he considered it his reason for living and found release in listening to recordings from his collection. His other major release was in drink, which he consumed copiously while in exile. He enjoyed military life as well, and though he had no great for love for the Empire he was content to serve it.<ref name="Empire Blues" />

Though Malloc was not proud of his role in the [[Battle of Montellian Serat]] and it pushed him to resign from the military, he took the action of executing the prisoners on his own initiative, not on direct orders. He was consumed by self-pity, both due to guilt over the deaths he had caused and his own loss of a stable life on Devaron.<ref name="Fact File" /> He remembered Devaron fondly and missed its scenery, its way of life, and its women.<ref name="Empire Blues" /> When he was finally confronted with death, he attempted to justify himself to both himself and Fett, but was plainly suffering from guilt.<ref name="The Last One Standing" />

Malloc did not have much respect for other sentients, especially Humans. He did not even care much for his family.<ref name="Empire Blues" /><ref name="The Last One Standing" /> Wuher was his one real friend on Tatooine.<ref name="Empire Blues" /> He did not enjoy killing for its own sake, however, and when his actions caused Slag Flats to come to her death, he felt bad about it.<ref name="Tatooine Manhunt" /> Malloc did believe in the concept of [[Grace]], however, requiring him to display such virtues as patience and restraint.<ref name="Empire Blues" />

Malloc was not especially ambitious; he was content to simply follow musicians before he settled on Tatooine, and when he arrived he made a career as an informant but did so without checking his sources or putting much effort into obtaining information.<ref name="Empire Blues" /><ref name="Galaxy Guide 7" /> The one thing that could provoke significant effort on his part was music and obtaining it; otherwise he was content to drink, listen to music, and live simply.<ref name="Empire Blues" />

==Behind the scenes==
Kardue'sai'Malloc originally appeared as an extra among the cantina aliens in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. Known by the on-set nicknames "Louie" and "the Devil," Malloc was filmed during the additional photography for the cut-away shots establishing the various denizens of the cantina. The mask worn to play the character was created by [[Rick Baker]].<ref name="Cantina Roll-Call">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> A Devaronian who was confirmed to be Malloc in the [[Star Wars Blog]] article ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special Cantina: Who's Who]]'' also appeared briefly in a cantina scene from ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''.<ref name="The Star Wars Holiday Special" />

Despite the on-set nicknames, no name was given to the character until ''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]'' was published in [[1989]], at which point he was identified as the largely harmless drunk Labria.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 1" /> With the publication of ''[[Empire Blues: The Devaronian's Tale]]'' in ''[[Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina]]'' in 1995, Labria was identified as the alias of Kardue'sai'Malloc, a dangerous war criminal. ''Empire Blues'' also retconned Labria's relationship with Oxbel, established in ''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]'', as being misinformation from an elaborate scam.<ref name="Empire Blues" /><ref name="Galaxy Guide 7" /> Malloc's fate was ultimately given in ''[[The Last One Standing: The Tale of Boba Fett]]'' in ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]''; the story was by [[Daniel Keys Moran]], the author of ''Empire Blues''.<ref name="The Last One Standing" /><ref name="Empire Blues" />
